title: serving-runtime-compat-matrix-lts-cadence-and-rollout-automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a machine-actionable semantic versioning and LTS cadence for the serving runtime, produce a compatibility matrix for runtime components (kernels, KV cache, admin APIs, model loader), and implement automated rollout gates and upgrade tooling to minimize customer disruption.
proposal_summary: Introduce a three-channel LTS model (Rapid, Stable, Extended), formalize component-level compatibility guarantees, add pre-flight compatibility checks and an upgrade assistant, and wire automated canary rollouts with rollback triggers tied to telemetry and integration tests.
compatibility_matrix: Principles: ABI compatibility for runtime-kernels and KV store must be preserved within patch/minor; breaking ABI changes require major version and coordinated rollout.

Components covered: runtime-core (scheduler, batching), runtime-kernels (operator/blas kernels), proto-schema (gRPC/messages), admin-api (control plane endpoints), kv-cache format, model-artifact schema.

Semantic mapping: patch -> bugfixes, no behavior changes; minor -> additive features, optional new flags; major -> any behavior change that invalidates previous serialized state, RPC contract change, or kernel ABI change.

Backward compatibility guarantees: runtime-core and proto-schema: backward-compatible across patch and minor; runtime-kernels: ABI forward/backwards preserved for patch/minor when using stable kernel ABI builds; kv-cache: read-forward allowed for minor only when migration helper present.
Forward compatibility guarantees: Older runtimes can read newer model artifacts only if compatibility flag present; otherwise model loader must perform schema downgrade during rollout.
Concrete rule: Any change that invalidates KV cache on-disk format requires a migration path OR is classified as major and gated to Extended LTS with 36-month support and dedicated migration tooling.
Compatibility labels: SAFE (no operator action), SOFT (requires feature flag/migration tool), HARD (requires coordinated major upgrade and communication).
Examples: Changing a kernel calling convention -> HARD/major. Adding a new optional admin-api field -> SAFE/minor. Removing a public RPC -> HARD/major and deprecation cycle required.
lts_cadence_and_channel_definitions: Channels: Rapid (6-month cadence, includes experimental non-breaking features, intended for early adopters), Stable (12-month cadence, recommended for production), Extended (36-month security/critical fixes only, for long-lived Dedicated/Private installations).
Release window: Stable receives one major per year; Rapid receives two feature majors per year. Extended is forked from a Stable major and receives only backported critical/bug/security fixes.
Support policy: Stable supported for 12 months after release; Extended supported for 36 months with paid Extended-support contracts; Rapid supported for 6 months.
Channel migration: Customers can opt-in to Rapid via console toggle; moving from Extended -> Stable -> Rapid is a forward upgrade path with compatibility checks required at each step.
Communication: Pursue a 90-day advance notice for any changes classified as HARD and publish migration guides and a deprecation timeline on the docs portal.
deprecation_and_breaking_change_policy: Deprecation window: For PUBLIC admin-api or RPCs: 90 days notice + deprecation flag in two consecutive releases (first marked deprecated, second removed), except security-critical removals which may be expedited with customer notifications.
Runtime flags: Introduce feature gates/flags for any non-trivial behavioral changes. Default should preserve legacy behavior until flags are flipped in a later release.
Automated detection: compatibility-checker will scan API usage and cached artifacts to estimate customer impact and surface high-risk instances before cutover.
Private deployments: Require an offline upgrade plan and explicit sign-off for any breaking change; we must provide migration tooling and runbook.
rollout_gates: Phases: internal-canary (10% infra), partner-canary (selected Dedicated customers), public-gradual (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%).
Gate metrics: latency p95 increase <= 15% OR absolute increase < 40ms; error-rate increase <= 2x baseline; successful integration test pass rate >= 99%.
Automated rollback triggers: sustained latency breach (over threshold for 5m), error spikes (+3x for 2m), regression test failures in live harness, telemetry anomaly scoring > 0.8.
Safety actions: automatic throttling to prior binary, circuit-break to previous model variant, and immediate on-call paging if rollback occurs.
Canary sizing: start with single AZ fraction then expand per metrics; Dedicated customer rollouts require opt-in unless change classified SAFE.
upgrade_tooling: rwt-compat-checker: CLI tool that validates a target cluster's running versions, on-disk KV cache signatures, and open RPC usages; exits with codes (0 OK, 1 warnings, 2 blocking incompatibilities).
runtime-upgrade-assistant: web-assisted wizard in Console to schedule staged upgrades, run preflight checks, and orchestrate canaries with automated metric-based progression or rollback.
kv-migrate: transactional offline/online migrator for KV cache formats with snapshot/rollback support; exposes a dry-run mode for performance estimate.
kernel-abi-test-suite: small harness that runs representative microbenchmarks and correctness checks against new kernel builds to detect subtle ABI pains before rollouts.
CI hooks: merge to release branch must run compat-checker and kernel-abi-test-suite; any blocking incompatibility must be triaged before release.
migration_and_private_deployment_notes: Private/VPC customers often have stricter upgrade windows; provide automated preflight artifact bundle and an offline migrator binary they can run behind firewall.
For on-prem: support staged image rollouts with per-node drain/evict hooks and an opt-in 'safety hold' where admin approves each stage.
Offer a Migration Concierge service for Extended customers to execute complex KV or model-schema migrations as part of Extended-support contract.
acceptance_criteria: A published compatibility matrix doc on the internal docs portal and a public summary in docs.redwood.ai describing LTS channels and support windows.
rwt-compat-checker prototype available in developer-tools repo with exit codes and documented usage.
A release checklist template that enforces compat-checker pass and kernel-abi-test-suite success before release branch merge.
An automated canary workflow in the Console that implements the rollout gates and rollback triggers described above.
